title: Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease Relationship Mileage Allowance for Kestrel Retail Customers
content:
# Relationship Program Bulletin — Mileage Allowance for Long-Standing Kestrel Retail Customers

**Rule.** For the excess mileage charge on a closed-end commercial unit of the Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease whose lease ended by a turn-in or by a recovery after an uncured default, the miles over are reduced by the mileage relationship allowance, never below zero: 2,000 miles where the business has a Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract, open or closed, funded 36 or more whole months before today, 1,000 miles where its earliest-funded Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract was funded 12 to 35 whole months before today, and none where it has no Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract funded at least 12 whole months before today.

**Which contracts and which entries.** The contracts are the Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contracts held by the business. What is read is the funding entry posted on each such contract and its date; a contract counts whether it is still open or already closed.

**Counting.** Whole months are counted from the funding date to today and are one fewer where today's day of the month is smaller than the funding date's. A funding falls within the last N whole months when fewer than N whole months separate its date from today; so a funding 36 or more whole months before today is outside the last 36 whole months.

## Allowance table

| Earliest funding of a Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract, in whole months before today | Mileage relationship allowance |
|---|---|
| 36 or more | 2,000 miles (2000) |
| 12 to 35 | 1,000 miles (1000) |
| fewer than 12, or no such contract funded | none |

## Cases (hypothetical)

1. The business has one retail installment contract funded 40 whole months ago and since paid off: 2,000 miles, because a closed contract counts.
2. Its only retail installment contract was funded 35 whole months ago: 1,000 miles. At 36 whole months: 2,000 miles.
3. Its only retail installment contract was funded 11 whole months ago: none. At 12 whole months: 1,000 miles.
4. Miles over of 600 with a 1,000-mile allowance become zero, never below zero.
